key_insight: A high-throughput DFT search found many previously unknown CuI-based ternary compounds that can function as stable, transparent p-type conductors, broadening the design rules beyond classic delafossites.
engineering_relevance: These materials could enable better transparent electrodes and hole-transport layers for transparent electronics and tandem photovoltaics by providing a larger pool of intrinsically p-type, optically transparent candidates.
method: Minima hopping was used to explore X–Cu–I ternary composition space.
Density functional theory screened candidates for thermodynamic stability, optical transparency, and light hole effective mass.
The resulting dataset was used to test and generalize chemical modulation of the valence band design rules.
evidence_signal: The study reports 58 p-type TCM candidates, 49 of them previously unreported, including 20 degenerate semiconductors; Cu2FI2 is highlighted with a 3.75 eV gap and 0.262 m0 hole effective mass.
watch_item: The findings are computationally predicted and still need experimental synthesis, phase stability validation, and device-level performance testing.
paper_title: High-throughput computational discovery of CuI-based ternary $p$-type transparent conductors
